docRequirement: `scheduled-tasks.md:35` binds us to ship `/loop` as a *bundled skill*: "The `/loop` [bundled skill](/docs/en/commands) is the quickest way to run a prompt on repeat while the session stays open. Both the interval and the prompt are optional, and what you provide determines how the loop behaves." The dispatch table at `:37`-`:41` fixes three behaviours: interval + prompt runs on a fixed schedule; prompt only runs "at an interval Claude chooses" each iteration; interval only or nothing runs the built-in maintenance prompt, "or your `loop.md` if one exists". `:58` fixes the interval grammar (leading bare token like `30m` or trailing clause like `every 2 hours`; units `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`), `:60` fixes seconds rounded up to a minute and non-cron-expressible intervals such as `7m` or `90m` rounded with Claude telling the user what it picked. `:52` puts the conversion in the model: "Claude converts it to a cron expression, schedules the job, and confirms the cadence and job ID." `:64` fixes the self-paced mode (a delay "between one minute and one hour", chosen delay and reason printed each iteration), `:74` exempts a dynamic loop from the jitter rules while keeping the seven-day expiry, `:100`-`:120` fix `loop.md` with `.claude/loop.md` taking precedence over `~/.claude/loop.md`, re-read each iteration and truncated past 25,000 bytes, `:82`-`:88` fix the built-in maintenance prompt's three ordered steps and its no-new-initiatives bound, `:128`-`:130` fix `Esc` clearing the pending wakeup and `ScheduleWakeup` with `stop: true`, and `:208` requires that `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1` make "the cron tools and `/loop`" unavailable together. `:43` additionally requires that a scheduled fire only execute skills Claude is allowed to invoke on its own, everything else reaching Claude as plain text.

userImpact: Typing `/loop 5m check the deploy` does nothing useful: `loop` is not among the commands `listCustomSlashCommandSummaries` returns (no `loop` directory under `apps/electron/resources/skills/`, no `loop.md` under any `COMMAND_DIRS` root at `custom-commands.ts:61`), so it never reaches the documented handler. What a user loses concretely: the documented entry point and its interval grammar; the built-in maintenance prompt behind a bare `/loop`; a project or user `loop.md` as the default loop prompt (a file a user creates is silently inert); the self-paced mode, so no Claude-chosen 1-minute-to-1-hour cadence and no printed delay-and-reason; and `Esc` as the way to stop a waiting loop. Partly mitigated, so the gap should not be overread: asking in natural language ("check the deploy every 5 minutes") does work — the model routes it to `CronCreate`, and the cron half is at parity — and `Monitor`, which `:72` names as the more token-efficient alternative to a dynamic loop, ships. One further concrete symptom independent of `/loop`: because every fire is delivered wrapped as `<task-notification>` data, a user who schedules `/review-pr 1234` every 20 minutes gets that literal text handed to the model each iteration instead of the skill executing, which is the opposite of `:43`'s rule for a skill Claude is allowed to invoke.
